correctness.rationale: A four-node irreducible reversible Jacobi matrix supplies the positive spectral measure. For each product the coefficient equals an explicit entry of R_m(J). Degree 0 and 1 are automatic; the other twelve coefficients have exact symbolic formulas independently checked with 35 exact assertions. For 0<r<1, the three potentially negative entries have positive factors times H,K,L; at r=1 the K factor vanishes and L>0 under H>=0. The all-ratio region follows by endpoint and one-sided limit necessities and explicit nonnegative lower bounds for H,K,L. Distinct nodes, open profile inequalities and endpoints are handled; finite numerics are not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Polzer (2026) explicitly asks for the all-constant-ratio positivity boundary, supplying a sufficient Newton-logconcavity theorem. The new four-node iff conditions include a profile with negative third Newton coefficient and so are not implied by that sufficient criterion. Szwarc (2003) gives general implicit necessary/sufficient machinery but not these closed-form N=3 parameter conditions. Comparisons with the accessible companion sources, relevant mathematical results and index searches returned no explicit equivalent cone. Risk of an older unindexed low-degree derivation is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The four-point constant-ratio system is the smallest family with two independent interior profile parameters and multiple coupled positivity obstructions. Classifying the full three-parameter positivity cone and the sharp universal-ratio profile region resolves a concrete low-dimensional instance of Polzer’s stated exact-boundary problem. The endpoint law and negative-Newton example explain a structural boundary of the available sufficient criterion. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary isolated computed coefficient.
